reason: Both conversations reached the correct 'normal anti-crease' conclusion without pushing parts or an engineer, but Conversation 1 got there with cleaner, more sensible opening questions (door shut, is the drum turning) that matched the right first step, and it correctly explained the door-switch behaviour. Conversation 2 repeatedly introduced a 'door won't unlock until cooled' concept that doesn't apply to tumble dryers, floated a 'control system fault' and an odd 'clicking sound' question early on, which muddied an otherwise simple case. Conversation 2 did better on naming 'anti-crease' explicitly and directly reassuring the homeowner about electricity use, while Conversation 1 had a slightly off 10-20 minute expectation and a generic fire-safety panel, so the margin is only slight.
